9/// \file
10/// This file contains the declarations of the Vectorization Plan base classes:
11/// 1. VPBasicBlock and VPRegionBlock that inherit from a common pure virtual
12/// VPBlockBase, together implementing a Hierarchical CFG;
13/// 2. Pure virtual VPRecipeBase serving as the base class for recipes contained
14/// within VPBasicBlocks;
15/// 3. Pure virtual VPSingleDefRecipe serving as a base class for recipes that
16/// also inherit from VPValue.
17/// 4. VPInstruction, a concrete Recipe and VPUser modeling a single planned
18/// instruction;
19/// 5. The VPlan class holding a candidate for vectorization;
20/// These are documented in docs/VectorizationPlan.rst.
21//
22//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

76/// \enum UncountableExitStyle
77/// Different methods of handling early exits.
78///
79enum class UncountableExitStyle {
80 NoUncountableExit = 0,
81 /// No side effects to worry about, so we can process any uncountable exits
82 /// in the loop and branch either to the middle block if the trip count was
83 /// reached, or an early exitblock to determine which exit was taken.
84 ReadOnly,
85 /// All memory operations other than the load(s) required to determine whether
86 /// an uncountable exit occurre will be masked based on that condition. If an
87 /// uncountable exit is taken, then all lanes before the exiting lane will
88 /// complete, leaving just the final lane to execute in the scalar tail.
89 MaskedHandleExitInScalarLoop,
90};

92/// VPBlockBase is the building block of the Hierarchical Control-Flow Graph.
93/// A VPBlockBase can be either a VPBasicBlock or a VPRegionBlock.
94class LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPBlockBase {
95 friend class VPBlockUtils;
96
97 /// An optional name for the block.
98 std::string Name;
99
100 /// The immediate VPRegionBlock which this VPBlockBase belongs to, or null if
101 /// it is a topmost VPBlockBase.
102 VPRegionBlock *Parent = nullptr;
103
104 /// List of predecessor blocks.
105 SmallVector<VPBlockBase *, 1> Predecessors;
106
107 /// List of successor blocks.
108 SmallVector<VPBlockBase *, 1> Successors;
109
110 /// VPlan containing the block. Can only be set on the entry block of the
111 /// plan.
112 VPlan *Plan = nullptr;
113
114 /// Add \p Successor as the last successor to this block.
115 void appendSuccessor(VPBlockBase *Successor) {
116 assert(Successor && "Cannot add nullptr successor!");
117 Successors.push_back(Successor);
118 }
119
120 /// Add \p Predecessor as the last predecessor to this block.
121 void appendPredecessor(VPBlockBase *Predecessor) {
122 assert(Predecessor && "Cannot add nullptr predecessor!");
123 Predecessors.push_back(Predecessor);
124 }
125
126 /// Remove \p Predecessor from the predecessors of this block.
127 void removePredecessor(VPBlockBase *Predecessor) {
128 auto Pos = find(Predecessors, Predecessor);
129 assert(Pos && "Predecessor does not exist");
130 Predecessors.erase(Pos);
131 }
132
133 /// Remove \p Successor from the successors of this block.
134 void removeSuccessor(VPBlockBase *Successor) {
135 auto Pos = find(Successors, Successor);
136 assert(Pos && "Successor does not exist");
137 Successors.erase(Pos);
138 }
139
140 /// This function replaces one predecessor with another, useful when
141 /// trying to replace an old block in the CFG with a new one.
142 void replacePredecessor(VPBlockBase *Old, VPBlockBase *New) {
143 auto I = find(Predecessors, Old);
144 assert(I != Predecessors.end());
145 assert(Old->getParent() == New->getParent() &&
146 "replaced predecessor must have the same parent");
147 *I = New;
148 }
149
150 /// This function replaces one successor with another, useful when
151 /// trying to replace an old block in the CFG with a new one.
152 void replaceSuccessor(VPBlockBase *Old, VPBlockBase *New) {
153 auto I = find(Successors, Old);
154 assert(I != Successors.end());
155 assert(Old->getParent() == New->getParent() &&
156 "replaced successor must have the same parent");
157 *I = New;
158 }
159
160public:
161 /// An enumeration for keeping track of the concrete subclass of VPBlockBase
162 /// that are actually instantiated. Values of this enumeration are kept in the
163 /// SubclassID field of the VPBlockBase objects. They are used for concrete
164 /// type identification.
165 using VPBlockTy = enum : unsigned char {
166 VPRegionBlockSC,
167 VPBasicBlockSC,
168 VPIRBasicBlockSC
169 };
170
171 using VPBlocksTy = SmallVectorImpl<VPBlockBase *>;
172
173 virtual ~VPBlockBase() = default;
174
175 const std::string &getName() const { return Name; }
176
177 void setName(const Twine &newName) { Name = newName.str(); }
178
179 /// \return an ID for the concrete type of this object.
180 /// This is used to implement the classof checks. This should not be used
181 /// for any other purpose, as the values may change as LLVM evolves.
182 unsigned getVPBlockID() const { return SubclassID; }
183
184 VPRegionBlock *getParent() { return Parent; }
185 const VPRegionBlock *getParent() const { return Parent; }
186
187 /// \return A pointer to the plan containing the current block.
188 VPlan *getPlan();
189 const VPlan *getPlan() const;
190
191 /// Sets the pointer of the plan containing the block. The block must be the
192 /// entry block into the VPlan.
193 void setPlan(VPlan *ParentPlan);
194
195 void setParent(VPRegionBlock *P) { Parent = P; }
196
197 /// \return the VPBasicBlock that is the entry of this VPBlockBase,
198 /// recursively, if the latter is a VPRegionBlock. Otherwise, if this
199 /// VPBlockBase is a VPBasicBlock, it is returned.
200 const VPBasicBlock *getEntryBasicBlock() const;
201 VPBasicBlock *getEntryBasicBlock();
202
203 /// \return the VPBasicBlock that is the exiting this VPBlockBase,
204 /// recursively, if the latter is a VPRegionBlock. Otherwise, if this
205 /// VPBlockBase is a VPBasicBlock, it is returned.
206 const VPBasicBlock *getExitingBasicBlock() const;
207 VPBasicBlock *getExitingBasicBlock();
208
209 const VPBlocksTy &getSuccessors() const { return Successors; }
210 VPBlocksTy &getSuccessors() { return Successors; }
211
212 /// Returns true if this block has any successors.
213 bool hasSuccessors() const { return !Successors.empty(); }
214 /// Returns true if this block has any predecessors.
215 bool hasPredecessors() const { return !Predecessors.empty(); }
216
217 iterator_range<VPBlockBase **> successors() { return Successors; }
218 iterator_range<VPBlockBase **> predecessors() { return Predecessors; }
219
220 const VPBlocksTy &getPredecessors() const { return Predecessors; }
221 VPBlocksTy &getPredecessors() { return Predecessors; }
222
223 /// \return the successor of this VPBlockBase if it has a single successor.
224 /// Otherwise return a null pointer.
225 VPBlockBase *getSingleSuccessor() const {
226 return (Successors.size() == 1 ? *Successors.begin() : nullptr);
227 }
228
229 /// \return the predecessor of this VPBlockBase if it has a single
230 /// predecessor. Otherwise return a null pointer.
231 VPBlockBase *getSinglePredecessor() const {
232 return (Predecessors.size() == 1 ? *Predecessors.begin() : nullptr);
233 }
234
235 size_t getNumSuccessors() const { return Successors.size(); }
236 size_t getNumPredecessors() const { return Predecessors.size(); }
237
238 /// An Enclosing Block of a block B is any block containing B, including B
239 /// itself. \return the closest enclosing block starting from "this", which
240 /// has successors. \return the root enclosing block if all enclosing blocks
241 /// have no successors.
242 VPBlockBase *getEnclosingBlockWithSuccessors();
243
244 /// \return the closest enclosing block starting from "this", which has
245 /// predecessors. \return the root enclosing block if all enclosing blocks
246 /// have no predecessors.
247 VPBlockBase *getEnclosingBlockWithPredecessors();
248
249 /// \return the successors either attached directly to this VPBlockBase or, if
250 /// this VPBlockBase is the exit block of a VPRegionBlock and has no
251 /// successors of its own, search recursively for the first enclosing
252 /// VPRegionBlock that has successors and return them. If no such
253 /// VPRegionBlock exists, return the (empty) successors of the topmost
254 /// VPBlockBase reached.
255 const VPBlocksTy &getHierarchicalSuccessors() {
256 return getEnclosingBlockWithSuccessors()->getSuccessors();
257 }
258
259 /// \return the predecessors either attached directly to this VPBlockBase or,
260 /// if this VPBlockBase is the entry block of a VPRegionBlock and has no
261 /// predecessors of its own, search recursively for the first enclosing
262 /// VPRegionBlock that has predecessors and return them. If no such
263 /// VPRegionBlock exists, return the (empty) predecessors of the topmost
264 /// VPBlockBase reached.
265 const VPBlocksTy &getHierarchicalPredecessors() {
266 return getEnclosingBlockWithPredecessors()->getPredecessors();
267 }
268
269 /// \return the hierarchical predecessor of this VPBlockBase if it has a
270 /// single hierarchical predecessor. Otherwise return a null pointer.
271 VPBlockBase *getSingleHierarchicalPredecessor() {
272 return getEnclosingBlockWithPredecessors()->getSinglePredecessor();
273 }
274
275 /// Set a given VPBlockBase \p Successor as the single successor of this
276 /// VPBlockBase. This VPBlockBase is not added as predecessor of \p Successor.
277 /// This VPBlockBase must have no successors.
278 void setOneSuccessor(VPBlockBase *Successor) {
279 assert(Successors.empty() && "Setting one successor when others exist.");
280 assert(Successor->getParent() == getParent() &&
281 "connected blocks must have the same parent");
282 appendSuccessor(Successor);
283 }
284
285 /// Set two given VPBlockBases \p IfTrue and \p IfFalse to be the two
286 /// successors of this VPBlockBase. This VPBlockBase is not added as
287 /// predecessor of \p IfTrue or \p IfFalse. This VPBlockBase must have no
288 /// successors.
289 void setTwoSuccessors(VPBlockBase *IfTrue, VPBlockBase *IfFalse) {
290 assert(Successors.empty() && "Setting two successors when others exist.");
291 appendSuccessor(IfTrue);
292 appendSuccessor(IfFalse);
293 }
294
295 /// Set each VPBasicBlock in \p NewPreds as predecessor of this VPBlockBase.
296 /// This VPBlockBase must have no predecessors. This VPBlockBase is not added
297 /// as successor of any VPBasicBlock in \p NewPreds.
298 void setPredecessors(ArrayRef<VPBlockBase *> NewPreds) {
299 assert(Predecessors.empty() && "Block predecessors already set.");
300 for (auto *Pred : NewPreds)
301 appendPredecessor(Pred);
302 }
303
304 /// Set each VPBasicBlock in \p NewSuccss as successor of this VPBlockBase.
305 /// This VPBlockBase must have no successors. This VPBlockBase is not added
306 /// as predecessor of any VPBasicBlock in \p NewSuccs.
307 void setSuccessors(ArrayRef<VPBlockBase *> NewSuccs) {
308 assert(Successors.empty() && "Block successors already set.");
309 for (auto *Succ : NewSuccs)
310 appendSuccessor(Succ);
311 }
312
313 /// Remove all the predecessor of this block.
314 void clearPredecessors() { Predecessors.clear(); }
315
316 /// Remove all the successors of this block.
317 void clearSuccessors() { Successors.clear(); }
318
319 /// Swap predecessors of the block. The block must have exactly 2
320 /// predecessors.
321 void swapPredecessors() {
322 assert(Predecessors.size() == 2 && "must have 2 predecessors to swap");
323 std::swap(Predecessors[0], Predecessors[1]);
324 }
325
326 /// Swap successors of the block. The block must have exactly 2 successors.
327 // TODO: This should be part of introducing conditional branch recipes rather
328 // than being independent.
329 void swapSuccessors() {
330 assert(Successors.size() == 2 && "must have 2 successors to swap");
331 std::swap(Successors[0], Successors[1]);
332 }
333
334 /// Returns the index for \p Pred in the blocks predecessors list.
335 unsigned getIndexForPredecessor(const VPBlockBase *Pred) const {
336 assert(count(Predecessors, Pred) == 1 &&
337 "must have Pred exactly once in Predecessors");
338 return std::distance(Predecessors.begin(), find(Predecessors, Pred));
339 }
340
341 /// Returns the index for \p Succ in the blocks successor list.
342 unsigned getIndexForSuccessor(const VPBlockBase *Succ) const {
343 assert(count(Successors, Succ) == 1 &&
344 "must have Succ exactly once in Successors");
345 return std::distance(Successors.begin(), find(Successors, Succ));
346 }
347
348 /// The method which generates the output IR that correspond to this
349 /// VPBlockBase, thereby "executing" the VPlan.
350 virtual void execute(VPTransformState *State) = 0;
351
352 /// Return the cost of the block.
353 virtual InstructionCost cost(ElementCount VF, VPCostContext &Ctx) = 0;
354
355#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
356 void printAsOperand(raw_ostream &OS, bool PrintType = false) const {
357 OS << getName();
358 }
359
360 /// Print plain-text dump of this VPBlockBase to \p O, prefixing all lines
361 /// with \p Indent. \p SlotTracker is used to print unnamed VPValue's using
362 /// consequtive numbers.
363 ///
364 /// Note that the numbering is applied to the whole VPlan, so printing
365 /// individual blocks is consistent with the whole VPlan printing.
366 virtual void print(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
367 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const = 0;
368
369 /// Print plain-text dump of this VPlan to \p O.
370 void print(raw_ostream &O) const;
371
372 /// Print the successors of this block to \p O, prefixing all lines with \p
373 /// Indent.
374 void printSuccessors(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent) const;
375
376 /// Dump this VPBlockBase to dbgs().
377 LLVM_DUMP_METHOD void dump() const { print(dbgs()); }
378#endif
379
380 /// Clone the current block and it's recipes without updating the operands of
381 /// the cloned recipes, including all blocks in the single-entry single-exit
382 /// region for VPRegionBlocks.
383 virtual VPBlockBase *clone() = 0;
384
385private:
386 const VPBlockTy SubclassID; ///< Subclass identifier (for isa/dyn_cast).
387
388protected:
389 VPBlockBase(VPBlockTy SC, const std::string &N) : Name(N), SubclassID(SC) {}
390};

392/// VPRecipeBase is a base class modeling a sequence of one or more output IR
393/// instructions. VPRecipeBase owns the VPValues it defines through VPDef
394/// and is responsible for deleting its defined values. Single-value
395/// recipes must inherit from VPSingleDef instead of inheriting from both
396/// VPRecipeBase and VPValue separately.
397class LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPRecipeBase
398 : public ilist_node_with_parent<VPRecipeBase, VPBasicBlock>,
399 public VPDef,
400 public VPUser {
401 friend VPBasicBlock;
402 friend class VPBlockUtils;
403
404 /// Each VPRecipe belongs to a single VPBasicBlock.
405 VPBasicBlock *Parent = nullptr;
406
407 /// The debug location for the recipe.
408 DebugLoc DL;
409
410public:
411 /// An enumeration for keeping track of the concrete subclass of VPRecipeBase
412 /// that is actually instantiated. Values of this enumeration are kept in the
413 /// SubclassID field of the VPRecipeBase objects. They are used for concrete
414 /// type identification.
415 using VPRecipeTy = enum : unsigned char {
416 VPBranchOnMaskSC,
417 VPDerivedIVSC,
418 VPExpandSCEVSC,
419 VPExpressionSC,
420 VPIRInstructionSC,
421 VPInstructionSC,
422 VPInterleaveEVLSC,
423 VPInterleaveSC,
424 VPReductionEVLSC,
425 VPReductionSC,
426 VPReplicateSC,
427 VPScalarIVStepsSC,
428 VPVectorPointerSC,
429 VPVectorEndPointerSC,
430 VPWidenCallSC,
431 VPWidenCanonicalIVSC,
432 VPWidenCastSC,
433 VPWidenGEPSC,
434 VPWidenIntrinsicSC,
435 VPWidenMemIntrinsicSC,
436 VPWidenLoadEVLSC,
437 VPWidenLoadSC,
438 VPWidenStoreEVLSC,
439 VPWidenStoreSC,
440 VPWidenSC,
441 VPBlendSC,
442 VPHistogramSC,
443 // START: Phi-like recipes. Need to be kept together.
444 VPWidenPHISC,
445 VPPredInstPHISC,
446 // START: SubclassID for recipes that inherit VPHeaderPHIRecipe.
447 // VPHeaderPHIRecipe need to be kept together.
448 VPCurrentIterationPHISC,
449 VPActiveLaneMaskPHISC,
450 VPFirstOrderRecurrencePHISC,
451 VPWidenIntOrFpInductionSC,
452 VPWidenPointerInductionSC,
453 VPReductionPHISC,
454 // END: SubclassID for recipes that inherit VPHeaderPHIRecipe
455 // END: Phi-like recipes
456 VPFirstPHISC = VPWidenPHISC,
457 VPFirstHeaderPHISC = VPCurrentIterationPHISC,
458 VPLastHeaderPHISC = VPReductionPHISC,
459 VPLastPHISC = VPReductionPHISC,
460 };

462 VPRecipeBase(VPRecipeTy SC, ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands,

464 : VPDef(), VPUser(Operands), DL(DL), SubclassID(SC) {}

466 ~VPRecipeBase() override = default;
467
468 /// Clone the current recipe.

470
471 /// \return the VPBasicBlock which this VPRecipe belongs to.

474
475 /// \return the VPRegionBlock which the recipe belongs to.

477 const VPRegionBlock *getRegion() const;
478
479 /// The method which generates the output IR instructions that correspond to
480 /// this VPRecipe, thereby "executing" the VPlan.
481 virtual void execute(VPTransformState &State) = 0;
482
483 /// Return the cost of this recipe, taking into account if the cost
484 /// computation should be skipped and the ForceTargetInstructionCost flag.

487
488 /// Insert an unlinked recipe into a basic block immediately before

515 iplist<VPRecipeBase>::iterator eraseFromParent();
516
517 /// \return an ID for the concrete type of this object.
518 VPRecipeTy getVPRecipeID() const { return SubclassID; }
519
520 /// Method to support type inquiry through isa, cast, and dyn_cast.
521 static inline bool classof(const VPDef *D) {
522 // All VPDefs are also VPRecipeBases.
523 return true;
524 }
525
526 static inline bool classof(const VPUser *U) { return true; }
527
528 /// Returns true if the recipe may have side-effects.
529 bool mayHaveSideEffects() const;
530
531 /// Return true if we can safely execute this recipe unconditionally even if
532 /// it is masked originally.
533 bool isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute() const;
534
535 /// Returns true for PHI-like recipes.
536 bool isPhi() const;
537
538 /// Returns true if the recipe may read from memory.
539 bool mayReadFromMemory() const;
540
541 /// Returns true if the recipe may write to memory.
542 bool mayWriteToMemory() const;
543
544 /// Returns true if the recipe may read from or write to memory.
545 bool mayReadOrWriteMemory() const {
546 return mayReadFromMemory() || mayWriteToMemory();
547 }
548
549 /// Returns the debug location of the recipe.
550 DebugLoc getDebugLoc() const { return DL; }
551
552 /// Set the recipe's debug location to \p NewDL.
553 void setDebugLoc(DebugLoc NewDL) { DL = NewDL; }
554
555#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
556 /// Dump the recipe to stderr (for debugging).
557 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST void dump() const;
558
559 /// Print the recipe, delegating to printRecipe().
560 void print(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
561 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const;
562#endif
563
564private:
565 /// Subclass identifier (for isa/dyn_cast).
566 const VPRecipeTy SubclassID;
567
568protected:
569 /// Compute the cost of this recipe either using a recipe's specialized
570 /// implementation or using the legacy cost model and the underlying
571 /// instructions.
572 virtual InstructionCost computeCost(ElementCount VF,
573 VPCostContext &Ctx) const;
574
575#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
576 /// Each concrete VPRecipe prints itself, without printing common information,
577 /// like debug info or metadata.
578 virtual void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
579 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const = 0;
580#endif
581};

583// Helper macro to define common classof implementations for recipes.
584#define VP_CLASSOF_IMPL(VPRecipeID) \
585 static inline bool classof(const VPRecipeBase *R) { \
586 return R->getVPRecipeID() == VPRecipeID; \
587 } \
588 static inline bool classof(const VPValue *V) { \
589 auto *R = V->getDefiningRecipe(); \
590 return R && R->getVPRecipeID() == VPRecipeID; \
591 } \
592 static inline bool classof(const VPUser *U) { \
593 auto *R = dyn_cast<VPRecipeBase>(U); \
594 return R && R->getVPRecipeID() == VPRecipeID; \
595 } \
596 static inline bool classof(const VPSingleDefRecipe *R) { \
597 return R->getVPRecipeID() == VPRecipeID; \
598 }

604/// VPSingleDefRecipe is a base class for recipes that model a sequence of one
605/// or more output IR that define a single result VPValue. Note that
606/// VPSingleDefRecipe must inherit from VPRecipeBase before VPSingleDefValue.
607class LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPSingleDefRecipe : public VPRecipeBase,
608 public VPSingleDefValue {
609public:
610 VPSingleDefRecipe(VPRecipeTy SC, ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands,
611 DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown())
612 : VPRecipeBase(SC, Operands, DL), VPSingleDefValue(this) {}
613
614 VPSingleDefRecipe(VPRecipeTy SC, ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands, Value *UV,
615 DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown())
616 : VPRecipeBase(SC, Operands, DL), VPSingleDefValue(this, UV) {}
617
618 VPSingleDefRecipe(VPRecipeTy SC, ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands, Type *ResultTy,
619 Value *UV = nullptr, DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown())
620 : VPRecipeBase(SC, Operands, DL), VPSingleDefValue(this, UV, ResultTy) {}
621
622 static inline bool classof(const VPRecipeBase *R) {
623 switch (R->getVPRecipeID()) {
624 case VPRecipeBase::VPDerivedIVSC:
625 case VPRecipeBase::VPExpandSCEVSC:
626 case VPRecipeBase::VPExpressionSC:
627 case VPRecipeBase::VPInstructionSC:
628 case VPRecipeBase::VPReductionEVLSC:
629 case VPRecipeBase::VPReductionSC:
630 case VPRecipeBase::VPReplicateSC:
631 case VPRecipeBase::VPScalarIVStepsSC:
632 case VPRecipeBase::VPVectorPointerSC:
633 case VPRecipeBase::VPVectorEndPointerSC:
634 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenCallSC:
635 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenCanonicalIVSC:
636 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenCastSC:
637 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenGEPSC:
638 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenIntrinsicSC:
639 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenMemIntrinsicSC:
640 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenSC:
641 case VPRecipeBase::VPBlendSC:
642 case VPRecipeBase::VPPredInstPHISC:
643 case VPRecipeBase::VPCurrentIterationPHISC:
644 case VPRecipeBase::VPActiveLaneMaskPHISC:
645 case VPRecipeBase::VPFirstOrderRecurrencePHISC:
646 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenPHISC:
647 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenIntOrFpInductionSC:
648 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenPointerInductionSC:
649 case VPRecipeBase::VPReductionPHISC:
650 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenLoadEVLSC:
651 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenLoadSC:
652 return true;
653 case VPRecipeBase::VPBranchOnMaskSC:
654 case VPRecipeBase::VPInterleaveEVLSC:
655 case VPRecipeBase::VPInterleaveSC:
656 case VPRecipeBase::VPIRInstructionSC:
657 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenStoreEVLSC:
658 case VPRecipeBase::VPWidenStoreSC:
659 case VPRecipeBase::VPHistogramSC:
660 return false;
661 }
662 llvm_unreachable("Unhandled VPRecipeID");
663 }
664
665 static inline bool classof(const VPValue *V) {
666 auto *R = V->getDefiningRecipe();
667 return R && classof(R);
668 }
669
670 static inline bool classof(const VPUser *U) {
671 auto *R = dyn_cast<VPRecipeBase>(U);
672 return R && classof(R);
673 }
674
675 VPSingleDefRecipe *clone() override = 0;
676
677 /// Returns the underlying instruction.
678 Instruction *getUnderlyingInstr() {
679 return cast<Instruction>(getUnderlyingValue());
680 }
681 const Instruction *getUnderlyingInstr() const {
682 return cast<Instruction>(getUnderlyingValue());
683 }
684
685#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
686 /// Print this VPSingleDefRecipe to dbgs() (for debugging).
687 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST LLVM_DUMP_METHOD void dump() const;
688#endif
689};

691/// Class to record and manage LLVM IR flags.
692LLVM_PACKED_START
693class VPIRFlags {
694 enum class OperationType : unsigned char {
695 Cmp,
696 FCmp,
697 OverflowingBinOp,
698 Trunc,
699 DisjointOp,
700 PossiblyExactOp,
701 GEPOp,
702 FPMathOp,
703 NonNegOp,
704 ReductionOp,
705 Other
706 };
707
708public:
709 struct WrapFlagsTy {
710 char HasNUW : 1;
711 char HasNSW : 1;
712
713 WrapFlagsTy(bool HasNUW, bool HasNSW) : HasNUW(HasNUW), HasNSW(HasNSW) {}
714 };
715
716 struct TruncFlagsTy {
717 char HasNUW : 1;
718 char HasNSW : 1;
719
720 TruncFlagsTy(bool HasNUW, bool HasNSW) : HasNUW(HasNUW), HasNSW(HasNSW) {}
721 };
722
723 struct DisjointFlagsTy {
724 char IsDisjoint : 1;
725 DisjointFlagsTy(bool IsDisjoint) : IsDisjoint(IsDisjoint) {}
726 };
727
728 struct NonNegFlagsTy {
729 char NonNeg : 1;
730 NonNegFlagsTy(bool IsNonNeg) : NonNeg(IsNonNeg) {}
731 };
732
733private:
734 struct ExactFlagsTy {
735 char IsExact : 1;
736 ExactFlagsTy(bool Exact) : IsExact(Exact) {}
737 };
738 struct FastMathFlagsTy {
739 char AllowReassoc : 1;
740 char NoNaNs : 1;
741 char NoInfs : 1;
742 char NoSignedZeros : 1;
743 char AllowReciprocal : 1;
744 char AllowContract : 1;
745 char ApproxFunc : 1;
746
747 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST FastMathFlagsTy(const FastMathFlags &FMF);
748 };
749 /// Holds both the predicate and fast-math flags for floating-point
750 /// comparisons.
751 struct FCmpFlagsTy {
752 uint8_t CmpPredStorage;
753 FastMathFlagsTy FMFs;
754 };
755 /// Holds reduction-specific flags: RecurKind, IsOrdered, IsInLoop, and FMFs.
756 struct ReductionFlagsTy {
757 // RecurKind has ~26 values, needs 5 bits but uses 6 bits to account for
758 // additional kinds.
759 unsigned char Kind : 6;
760 // TODO: Derive order/in-loop from plan and remove here.
761 unsigned char IsOrdered : 1;
762 unsigned char IsInLoop : 1;
763 FastMathFlagsTy FMFs;
764
765 ReductionFlagsTy(RecurKind Kind, bool IsOrdered, bool IsInLoop,
766 FastMathFlags FMFs)
767 : Kind(static_cast<unsigned char>(Kind)), IsOrdered(IsOrdered),
768 IsInLoop(IsInLoop), FMFs(FMFs) {}
769 };
770
771 OperationType OpType;
772
773 union {
774 uint8_t CmpPredStorage;
775 WrapFlagsTy WrapFlags;
776 TruncFlagsTy TruncFlags;
777 DisjointFlagsTy DisjointFlags;
778 ExactFlagsTy ExactFlags;
779 uint8_t GEPFlagsStorage;
780 NonNegFlagsTy NonNegFlags;
781 FastMathFlagsTy FMFs;
782 FCmpFlagsTy FCmpFlags;
783 ReductionFlagsTy ReductionFlags;
784 uint8_t AllFlags[2];
785 };
786
787public:
788 VPIRFlags() : OpType(OperationType::Other), AllFlags() {}
789
790 VPIRFlags(Instruction &I) : VPIRFlags() {
791 if (auto *FCmp = dyn_cast<FCmpInst>(&I)) {
792 OpType = OperationType::FCmp;
793 Bitfield::set<CmpInst::PredicateField>(FCmpFlags.CmpPredStorage,
794 FCmp->getPredicate());
795 assert(getPredicate() == FCmp->getPredicate() && "predicate truncated");
796 FCmpFlags.FMFs = FCmp->getFastMathFlags();
797 } else if (auto *Op = dyn_cast<CmpInst>(&I)) {
798 OpType = OperationType::Cmp;
799 Bitfield::set<CmpInst::PredicateField>(CmpPredStorage,
800 Op->getPredicate());
801 assert(getPredicate() == Op->getPredicate() && "predicate truncated");
802 } else if (auto *Op = dyn_cast<PossiblyDisjointInst>(&I)) {
803 OpType = OperationType::DisjointOp;
804 DisjointFlags.IsDisjoint = Op->isDisjoint();
805 } else if (auto *Op = dyn_cast<OverflowingBinaryOperator>(&I)) {
806 OpType = OperationType::OverflowingBinOp;
807 WrapFlags = {Op->hasNoUnsignedWrap(), Op->hasNoSignedWrap()};
808 } else if (auto *Op = dyn_cast<TruncInst>(&I)) {
809 OpType = OperationType::Trunc;
810 TruncFlags = {Op->hasNoUnsignedWrap(), Op->hasNoSignedWrap()};
811 } else if (auto *Op = dyn_cast<PossiblyExactOperator>(&I)) {
812 OpType = OperationType::PossiblyExactOp;
813 ExactFlags.IsExact = Op->isExact();
814 } else if (auto *GEP = dyn_cast<GetElementPtrInst>(&I)) {
815 OpType = OperationType::GEPOp;
816 GEPFlagsStorage = GEP->getNoWrapFlags().getRaw();
817 assert(getGEPNoWrapFlags() == GEP->getNoWrapFlags() &&
818 "wrap flags truncated");
819 } else if (auto *PNNI = dyn_cast<PossiblyNonNegInst>(&I)) {
820 OpType = OperationType::NonNegOp;
821 NonNegFlags.NonNeg = PNNI->hasNonNeg();
822 } else if (auto *Op = dyn_cast<FPMathOperator>(&I)) {
823 OpType = OperationType::FPMathOp;
824 FMFs = Op->getFastMathFlags();
825 }
826 }
827
828 VPIRFlags(CmpInst::Predicate Pred) : OpType(OperationType::Cmp), AllFlags() {
829 Bitfield::set<CmpInst::PredicateField>(CmpPredStorage, Pred);
830 assert(getPredicate() == Pred && "predicate truncated");
831 }
832
833 VPIRFlags(CmpInst::Predicate Pred, FastMathFlags FMFs)
834 : OpType(OperationType::FCmp), AllFlags() {
835 Bitfield::set<CmpInst::PredicateField>(FCmpFlags.CmpPredStorage, Pred);
836 assert(getPredicate() == Pred && "predicate truncated");
837 FCmpFlags.FMFs = FMFs;
838 }
839
840 VPIRFlags(WrapFlagsTy WrapFlags)
841 : OpType(OperationType::OverflowingBinOp), AllFlags() {
842 this->WrapFlags = WrapFlags;
843 }
844
845 VPIRFlags(TruncFlagsTy TruncFlags)
846 : OpType(OperationType::Trunc), AllFlags() {
847 this->TruncFlags = TruncFlags;
848 }
849
850 VPIRFlags(FastMathFlags FMFs) : OpType(OperationType::FPMathOp), AllFlags() {
851 this->FMFs = FMFs;
852 }
853
854 VPIRFlags(DisjointFlagsTy DisjointFlags)
855 : OpType(OperationType::DisjointOp), AllFlags() {
856 this->DisjointFlags = DisjointFlags;
857 }
858
859 VPIRFlags(NonNegFlagsTy NonNegFlags)
860 : OpType(OperationType::NonNegOp), AllFlags() {
861 this->NonNegFlags = NonNegFlags;
862 }
863
864 VPIRFlags(ExactFlagsTy ExactFlags)
865 : OpType(OperationType::PossiblyExactOp), AllFlags() {
866 this->ExactFlags = ExactFlags;
867 }
868
869 VPIRFlags(GEPNoWrapFlags GEPFlags)
870 : OpType(OperationType::GEPOp), AllFlags() {
871 GEPFlagsStorage = GEPFlags.getRaw();
872 }
873
874 VPIRFlags(RecurKind Kind, bool IsOrdered, bool IsInLoop, FastMathFlags FMFs)
875 : OpType(OperationType::ReductionOp), AllFlags() {
876 ReductionFlags = ReductionFlagsTy(Kind, IsOrdered, IsInLoop, FMFs);
877 }
878
879 void transferFlags(VPIRFlags &Other) {
880 OpType = Other.OpType;
881 AllFlags[0] = Other.AllFlags[0];
882 AllFlags[1] = Other.AllFlags[1];
883 }
884
885 /// Only keep flags also present in \p Other. \p Other must have the same
886 /// OpType as the current object.
887 void intersectFlags(const VPIRFlags &Other);
888
889 /// Drop all poison-generating flags.
890 void dropPoisonGeneratingFlags() {
891 // NOTE: This needs to be kept in-sync with
892 // Instruction::dropPoisonGeneratingFlags.
893 switch (OpType) {
894 case OperationType::OverflowingBinOp:
895 WrapFlags.HasNUW = false;
896 WrapFlags.HasNSW = false;
897 break;
898 case OperationType::Trunc:
899 TruncFlags.HasNUW = false;
900 TruncFlags.HasNSW = false;
901 break;
902 case OperationType::DisjointOp:
903 DisjointFlags.IsDisjoint = false;
904 break;
905 case OperationType::PossiblyExactOp:
906 ExactFlags.IsExact = false;
907 break;
908 case OperationType::GEPOp:
909 GEPFlagsStorage = 0;
910 break;
911 case OperationType::FPMathOp:
912 case OperationType::FCmp:
913 case OperationType::ReductionOp:
914 getFMFsRef().NoNaNs = false;
915 getFMFsRef().NoInfs = false;
916 break;
917 case OperationType::NonNegOp:
918 NonNegFlags.NonNeg = false;
919 break;
920 case OperationType::Cmp:
921 case OperationType::Other:
922 break;
923 }
924 }
925
926 /// Apply the IR flags to \p I.
927 void applyFlags(Instruction &I) const {
928 switch (OpType) {
929 case OperationType::OverflowingBinOp:
930 I.setHasNoUnsignedWrap(WrapFlags.HasNUW);
931 I.setHasNoSignedWrap(WrapFlags.HasNSW);
932 break;
933 case OperationType::Trunc:
934 I.setHasNoUnsignedWrap(TruncFlags.HasNUW);
935 I.setHasNoSignedWrap(TruncFlags.HasNSW);
936 break;
937 case OperationType::DisjointOp:
938 cast<PossiblyDisjointInst>(&I)->setIsDisjoint(DisjointFlags.IsDisjoint);
939 break;
940 case OperationType::PossiblyExactOp:
941 I.setIsExact(ExactFlags.IsExact);
942 break;
943 case OperationType::GEPOp:
944 cast<GetElementPtrInst>(&I)->setNoWrapFlags(
945 GEPNoWrapFlags::fromRaw(GEPFlagsStorage));
946 break;
947 case OperationType::FPMathOp:
948 case OperationType::FCmp: {
949 const FastMathFlagsTy &F = getFMFsRef();
950 I.setHasAllowReassoc(F.AllowReassoc);
951 I.setHasNoNaNs(F.NoNaNs);
952 I.setHasNoInfs(F.NoInfs);
953 I.setHasNoSignedZeros(F.NoSignedZeros);
954 I.setHasAllowReciprocal(F.AllowReciprocal);
955 I.setHasAllowContract(F.AllowContract);
956 I.setHasApproxFunc(F.ApproxFunc);
957 break;
958 }
959 case OperationType::NonNegOp:
960 I.setNonNeg(NonNegFlags.NonNeg);
961 break;
962 case OperationType::ReductionOp:
963 llvm_unreachable("reduction ops should not use applyFlags");
964 case OperationType::Cmp:
965 case OperationType::Other:
966 break;
967 }
968 }
969
970 CmpInst::Predicate getPredicate() const {
971 assert((OpType == OperationType::Cmp || OpType == OperationType::FCmp) &&
972 "recipe doesn't have a compare predicate");
973 uint8_t Storage = OpType == OperationType::FCmp ? FCmpFlags.CmpPredStorage
974 : CmpPredStorage;
975 return Bitfield::get<CmpInst::PredicateField>(Storage);
976 }
977
978 void setPredicate(CmpInst::Predicate Pred) {
979 assert((OpType == OperationType::Cmp || OpType == OperationType::FCmp) &&
980 "recipe doesn't have a compare predicate");
981 if (OpType == OperationType::FCmp)
982 Bitfield::set<CmpInst::PredicateField>(FCmpFlags.CmpPredStorage, Pred);
983 else
984 Bitfield::set<CmpInst::PredicateField>(CmpPredStorage, Pred);
985 assert(getPredicate() == Pred && "predicate truncated");
986 }
987
988 GEPNoWrapFlags getGEPNoWrapFlags() const {
989 return GEPNoWrapFlags::fromRaw(GEPFlagsStorage);
990 }
991
992 /// Returns true if the recipe has a comparison predicate.
993 bool hasPredicate() const {
994 return OpType == OperationType::Cmp || OpType == OperationType::FCmp;
995 }
996
997 /// Returns true if the recipe has fast-math flags.
998 bool hasFastMathFlags() const {
999 return OpType == OperationType::FPMathOp || OpType == OperationType::FCmp ||
1000 OpType == OperationType::ReductionOp;
1001 }
1002
1003 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST FastMathFlags getFastMathFlagsOrNone() const;
1004
1005 bool isNonNeg() const {
1006 assert(OpType == OperationType::NonNegOp &&
1007 "recipe doesn't have a NNEG flag");
1008 return NonNegFlags.NonNeg;
1009 }
1010
1011 bool hasNoUnsignedWrap() const {
1012 switch (OpType) {
1013 case OperationType::OverflowingBinOp:
1014 return WrapFlags.HasNUW;
1015 case OperationType::Trunc:
1016 return TruncFlags.HasNUW;
1017 default:
1018 llvm_unreachable("recipe doesn't have a NUW flag");
1019 }
1020 }
1021
1022 bool hasNoSignedWrap() const {
1023 switch (OpType) {
1024 case OperationType::OverflowingBinOp:
1025 return WrapFlags.HasNSW;
1026 case OperationType::Trunc:
1027 return TruncFlags.HasNSW;
1028 default:
1029 llvm_unreachable("recipe doesn't have a NSW flag");
1030 }
1031 }
1032
1033 bool hasNoWrapFlags() const {
1034 switch (OpType) {
1035 case OperationType::OverflowingBinOp:
1036 case OperationType::Trunc:
1037 return true;
1038 default:
1039 return false;
1040 }
1041 }
1042
1043 WrapFlagsTy getNoWrapFlags() const {
1044 return {hasNoUnsignedWrap(), hasNoSignedWrap()};
1045 }
1046
1047 bool isDisjoint() const {
1048 assert(OpType == OperationType::DisjointOp &&
1049 "recipe cannot have a disjoing flag");
1050 return DisjointFlags.IsDisjoint;
1051 }
1052
1053 RecurKind getRecurKind() const {
1054 assert(OpType == OperationType::ReductionOp &&
1055 "recipe doesn't have reduction flags");
1056 return static_cast<RecurKind>(ReductionFlags.Kind);
1057 }
1058
1059 bool isReductionOrdered() const {
1060 assert(OpType == OperationType::ReductionOp &&
1061 "recipe doesn't have reduction flags");
1062 return ReductionFlags.IsOrdered;
1063 }
1064
1065 bool isReductionInLoop() const {
1066 assert(OpType == OperationType::ReductionOp &&
1067 "recipe doesn't have reduction flags");
1068 return ReductionFlags.IsInLoop;
1069 }
1070
1071private:
1072 /// Get a reference to the fast-math flags for FPMathOp, FCmp or ReductionOp.
1073 FastMathFlagsTy &getFMFsRef() {
1074 if (OpType == OperationType::FCmp)
1075 return FCmpFlags.FMFs;
1076 if (OpType == OperationType::ReductionOp)
1077 return ReductionFlags.FMFs;
1078 return FMFs;
1079 }
1080 const FastMathFlagsTy &getFMFsRef() const {
1081 if (OpType == OperationType::FCmp)
1082 return FCmpFlags.FMFs;
1083 if (OpType == OperationType::ReductionOp)
1084 return ReductionFlags.FMFs;
1085 return FMFs;
1086 }
1087
1088public:
1089 /// Returns default flags for \p Opcode and scalar \p ResultTy for opcodes
1090 /// that support it, asserts otherwise. Opcodes not supporting default flags
1091 /// include compares and ComputeReductionResult.
1092 static VPIRFlags getDefaultFlags(unsigned Opcode, Type *ResultTy = nullptr);
1093
1094#if !defined(NDEBUG)
1095 /// Returns true if the set flags are valid for \p Opcode.
1096 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST bool flagsValidForOpcode(unsigned Opcode) const;
1097
1098 /// Returns true if \p Opcode has its required flags set.
1099 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST bool hasRequiredFlagsForOpcode(unsigned Opcode) const;
1100#endif
1101
1102#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1103 void printFlags(raw_ostream &O) const;
1104#endif
1105};
1106LLVM_PACKED_END
1107
1108static_assert(sizeof(VPIRFlags) <= 3, "VPIRFlags should not grow");

1164/// Helper to manage IR metadata for recipes. It filters out metadata that
1165/// cannot be propagated.
1166class LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPIRMetadata {
1167 SmallVector<std::pair<unsigned, MDNode *>> Metadata;
1168
1169public:
1170 VPIRMetadata() = default;
1171
1172 /// Adds metatadata that can be preserved from the original instruction
1173 /// \p I.
1174 VPIRMetadata(Instruction &I) { getMetadataToPropagate(&I, Metadata); }
1175
1176 /// Copy constructor for cloning.
1177 VPIRMetadata(const VPIRMetadata &Other) = default;
1178
1179 VPIRMetadata &operator=(const VPIRMetadata &Other) = default;
1180
1181 /// Add all metadata to \p I.
1182 void applyMetadata(Instruction &I) const;
1183
1184 /// Set metadata with kind \p Kind to \p Node. If metadata with \p Kind
1185 /// already exists, it will be replaced. Otherwise, it will be added.
1186 void setMetadata(unsigned Kind, MDNode *Node) {
1187 auto It =
1188 llvm::find_if(Metadata, [Kind](const std::pair<unsigned, MDNode *> &P) {
1189 return P.first == Kind;
1190 });
1191 if (It != Metadata.end())
1192 It->second = Node;
1193 else
1194 Metadata.emplace_back(Kind, Node);
1195 }
1196
1197 /// Intersect this VPIRMetadata object with \p MD, keeping only metadata
1198 /// nodes that are common to both.
1199 void intersect(const VPIRMetadata &MD);
1200
1201 /// Get metadata of kind \p Kind. Returns nullptr if not found.
1202 MDNode *getMetadata(unsigned Kind) const {
1203 auto It =
1204 find_if(Metadata, [Kind](const auto &P) { return P.first == Kind; });
1205 return It != Metadata.end() ? It->second : nullptr;
1206 }
1207
1208#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1209 /// Print metadata with node IDs.
1210 void print(raw_ostream &O, VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const;
1211#endif
1212};

1214/// This is a concrete Recipe that models a single VPlan-level instruction.
1215/// While as any Recipe it may generate a sequence of IR instructions when
1216/// executed, these instructions would always form a single-def expression as
1217/// the VPInstruction is also a single def-use vertex. Most VPInstruction
1218/// opcodes can take an optional mask. Masks may be assigned during
1219/// predication.
1220class LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPInstruction : public VPRecipeWithIRFlags,
1221 public VPIRMetadata {
1222public:
1223 /// VPlan opcodes, extending LLVM IR with idiomatics instructions.
1224 enum {
1225 FirstOrderRecurrenceSplice =
1226 Instruction::OtherOpsEnd + 1, // Combines the incoming and previous
1227 // values of a first-order recurrence.
1228 Not,
1229 // Creates a mask where each lane is active (true) whilst the current
1230 // counter (first operand + index) is less than the second operand. i.e.
1231 // mask[i] = icmpt ult (op0 + i), op1
1232 // The size of the mask returned is VF * Multiplier (UF, third op).
1233 ActiveLaneMask,
1234 ExplicitVectorLength,
1235 // Represents the incoming loop-invariant alias-mask. All memory accesses
1236 // in the loop must stay within the active lanes.
1237 IncomingAliasMask,
1238 CalculateTripCountMinusVF,
1239 // Increment the canonical IV separately for each unrolled part.
1240 CanonicalIVIncrementForPart,
1241 // Abstract instruction that compares two values and branches. This is
1242 // lowered to ICmp + BranchOnCond during VPlan to VPlan transformation.
1243 BranchOnCount,
1244 BranchOnCond,
1245 // Branch with 2 boolean condition operands and 3 successors. If condition
1246 // 0 is true, branches to successor 0; if condition 1 is true, branches to
1247 // successor 1; otherwise branches to successor 2. Expanded after region
1248 // dissolution into: (1) an OR of the two conditions branching to
1249 // middle.split or successor 2, and (2) middle.split branching to successor
1250 // 0 or successor 1 based on condition 0.
1251 BranchOnTwoConds,
1252 Broadcast,
1253 /// Given operands of (the same) struct type, creates a struct of fixed-
1254 /// width vectors each containing a struct field of all operands. The
1255 /// number of operands matches the element count of every vector.
1256 BuildStructVector,
1257 /// Creates a fixed-width vector containing all operands. The number of
1258 /// operands matches the vector element count.
1259 BuildVector,
1260 /// Extracts all lanes from its (non-scalable) vector operand. This is an
1261 /// abstract VPInstruction whose single defined VPValue represents VF
1262 /// scalars extracted from a vector, to be replaced by VF ExtractElement
1263 /// VPInstructions.
1264 Unpack,
1265 /// Reduce the operands to the final reduction result using the operation
1266 /// specified via the operation's VPIRFlags.
1267 ComputeReductionResult,
1268 // Extracts the last part of its operand. Removed during unrolling.
1269 ExtractLastPart,
1270 // Extracts the last lane of its vector operand, per part.
1271 ExtractLastLane,
1272 // Extracts the second-to-last lane from its operand or the second-to-last
1273 // part if it is scalar. In the latter case, the recipe will be removed
1274 // during unrolling.
1275 ExtractPenultimateElement,
1276 LogicalAnd, // Non-poison propagating logical And.
1277 LogicalOr, // Non-poison propagating logical Or.
1278 NumActiveLanes, // Counts the number of active lanes in a mask.
1279 // Add an offset in bytes (second operand) to a base pointer (first
1280 // operand). Only generates scalar values (either for the first lane only or
1281 // for all lanes, depending on its uses).
1282 PtrAdd,
1283 // Add a vector offset in bytes (second operand) to a scalar base pointer
1284 // (first operand).
1285 WidePtrAdd,
1286 // Returns a scalar boolean value, which is true if any lane of its
1287 // (boolean) vector operands is true. It produces the reduced value across
1288 // all unrolled iterations. Unrolling will add all copies of its original
1289 // operand as additional operands. AnyOf is poison-safe as all operands
1290 // will be frozen.
1291 AnyOf,
1292 // Calculates the first active lane index of the vector predicate operands.
1293 // It produces the lane index across all unrolled iterations. Unrolling will
1294 // add all copies of its original operand as additional operands.
1295 // Implemented with @llvm.experimental.cttz.elts, but returns the expected
1296 // result even with operands that are all zeroes.
1297 FirstActiveLane,
1298 // Calculates the last active lane index of the vector predicate operands.
1299 // The predicates must be prefix-masks (all 1s before all 0s). Used when
1300 // tail-folding to extract the correct live-out value from the last active
1301 // iteration. It produces the lane index across all unrolled iterations.
1302 // Unrolling will add all copies of its original operand as additional
1303 // operands.
1304 LastActiveLane,
1305 // Returns a reversed vector for the operand.
1306 Reverse,
1307 /// Start vector for reductions with 3 operands: the original start value,
1308 /// the identity value for the reduction and an integer indicating the
1309 /// scaling factor.
1310 ReductionStartVector,
1311 /// Extracts a single lane (first operand) from a set of vector operands.
1312 /// The lane specifies an index into a vector formed by combining all vector
1313 /// operands (all operands after the first one).
1314 ExtractLane,
1315 /// Explicit user for the resume phi of the canonical induction in the main
1316 /// VPlan, used by the epilogue vector loop.
1317 ResumeForEpilogue,
1318 /// Extracts the last active lane from a set of vectors. The first operand
1319 /// is the default value if no lanes in the masks are active. Conceptually,
1320 /// this concatenates all data vectors (odd operands), concatenates all
1321 /// masks (even operands -- ignoring the default value), and returns the
1322 /// last active value from the combined data vector using the combined mask.
1323 ExtractLastActive,
1324 /// Compute the exiting value of a wide induction after vectorization, that
1325 /// is the value of the last lane of the induction increment (i.e. its
1326 /// backedge value). Has the wide induction recipe as operand.
1327 ExitingIVValue,
1328 MaskedCond,
1329
1330 // The opcodes below are used for VPInstructionWithType.
1331 // NOTE: VPInstructionWithType classes are also used for:
1332 // 1. All CastInst variants - see createVPInstructionsForVPBB, and other
1333 // cases where createScalarCast, createScalarZExtOrTrunc and
1334 // createScalarSExtOrTrunc are invoked.
1335 // 2. Scalar load instructions - see createVPInstructionsForVPBB.
1336
1337 /// Scale the first operand (vector step) by the second operand
1338 /// (scalar-step). Casts both operands to the result type if needed.
1339 WideIVStep,
1340 // Creates a step vector starting from 0 to VF with a step of 1.
1341 StepVector,
1342 /// Calls a scalar intrinsic. The intrinsic ID is the last operand.
1343 Intrinsic,
1344
1345 OpsEnd = Intrinsic,
1346 };
1347
1348 /// Returns true if this VPInstruction generates scalar values for all lanes.
1349 /// Most VPInstructions generate a single value per part, either vector or
1350 /// scalar. VPReplicateRecipe takes care of generating multiple (scalar)
1351 /// values per all lanes, stemming from an original ingredient. This method
1352 /// identifies the (rare) cases of VPInstructions that do so as well, w/o an
1353 /// underlying ingredient.
1354 bool doesGeneratePerAllLanes() const;
1355
1356 /// Return the number of operands determined by the opcode of the
1357 /// VPInstruction, excluding mask. Returns -1u if the number of operands
1358 /// cannot be determined directly by the opcode.
1359 unsigned getNumOperandsForOpcode() const;
1360
1361private:
1362 typedef unsigned char OpcodeTy;
1363 OpcodeTy Opcode;
1364
1365 /// An optional name that can be used for the generated IR instruction.
1366 std::string Name;
1367
1368 /// Returns true if we can generate a scalar for the first lane only if
1369 /// needed.
1370 bool canGenerateScalarForFirstLane() const;
1371
1372 /// Utility methods serving execute(): generates a single vector instance of
1373 /// the modeled instruction. \returns the generated value. . In some cases an
1374 /// existing value is returned rather than a generated one.
1375 Value *generate(VPTransformState &State);
1376
1377 /// Returns true if the VPInstruction does not need masking.
1378 bool alwaysUnmasked() const {
1379 if (Opcode == VPInstruction::MaskedCond)
1380 return false;
1381
1382 // For now only VPInstructions with underlying values use masks.
1383 // TODO: provide masks to VPInstructions w/o underlying values.
1384 if (!getUnderlyingValue())
1385 return true;
1386
1387 return Instruction::isCast(Opcode) || Opcode == Instruction::PHI ||
1388 Opcode == Instruction::GetElementPtr;
1389 }
1390
1391public:
1392 VPInstruction(unsigned Opcode, ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands,
1393 const VPIRFlags &Flags = {}, const VPIRMetadata &MD = {},
1394 DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown(), const Twine &Name = "",
1395 Type *ResultTy = nullptr);
1396
1397 VP_CLASSOF_IMPL(VPRecipeBase::VPInstructionSC)
1398
1399 VPInstruction *clone() override {
1400 return cloneWithOperands(operands(), getScalarType());
1401 }
1402
1403 VPInstruction *cloneWithOperands(ArrayRef<VPValue *> NewOperands,
1404 Type *ResultTy = nullptr) {
1405 auto *New = new VPInstruction(Opcode, NewOperands, *this, *this,
1406 getDebugLoc(), Name, ResultTy);
1407 if (getUnderlyingValue())
1408 New->setUnderlyingValue(getUnderlyingInstr());
1409 return New;
1410 }
1411
1412 unsigned getOpcode() const { return Opcode; }
1413
1414 /// Add \p Op as operand of this VPInstruction. Only supported for AnyOf,
1415 /// ComputeReductionResult, BuildVector, BuildStructVector, ExtractLane,
1416 /// ExtractLastActive, FirstActiveLane, LastActiveLane.
1417 void addOperand(VPValue *Op);
1418
1419 /// Generate the instruction.
1420 /// TODO: We currently execute only per-part unless a specific instance is
1421 /// provided.
1422 void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
1423
1424 /// Return the cost of this VPInstruction.
1425 InstructionCost computeCost(ElementCount VF,
1426 VPCostContext &Ctx) const override;
1427
1428#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1429 /// Print the VPInstruction to dbgs() (for debugging).
1430 LLVM_DUMP_METHOD void dump() const;
1431#endif
1432
1433 bool hasResult() const {
1434 // CallInst may or may not have a result, depending on the called function.
1435 // Conservatively return calls have results for now.
1436 switch (getOpcode()) {
1437 case Instruction::Ret:
1438 case Instruction::UncondBr:
1439 case Instruction::CondBr:
1440 case Instruction::Store:
1441 case Instruction::Switch:
1442 case Instruction::IndirectBr:
1443 case Instruction::Resume:
1444 case Instruction::CatchRet:
1445 case Instruction::Unreachable:
1446 case Instruction::Fence:
1447 case Instruction::AtomicRMW:
1448 case VPInstruction::BranchOnCond:
1449 case VPInstruction::BranchOnTwoConds:
1450 case VPInstruction::BranchOnCount:
1451 return false;
1452 default:
1453 return true;
1454 }
1455 }
1456
1457 /// Returns true if the VPInstruction has a mask operand.
1458 bool isMasked() const {
1459 unsigned NumOpsForOpcode = getNumOperandsForOpcode();
1460 // VPInstructions without a fixed number of operands cannot be masked.
1461 if (NumOpsForOpcode == -1u)
1462 return false;
1463 return NumOpsForOpcode + 1 == getNumOperands();
1464 }
1465
1466 /// Returns the number of operands, excluding the mask if the VPInstruction is
1467 /// masked.
1468 unsigned getNumOperandsWithoutMask() const {
1469 return getNumOperands() - isMasked();
1470 }
1471
1472 /// Add mask \p Mask to an unmasked VPInstruction, if it needs masking.
1473 void addMask(VPValue *Mask) {
1474 assert(!isMasked() && "recipe is already masked");
1475 if (alwaysUnmasked())
1476 return;
1477 assert(Mask->getScalarType()->isIntegerTy(1) &&
1478 "Mask must be an i1 (vector)");
1479 VPUser::addOperand(Mask);
1480 }
1481
1482 /// Returns the mask for the VPInstruction. Returns nullptr for unmasked
1483 /// VPInstructions.
1484 VPValue *getMask() const {
1485 return isMasked() ? getOperand(getNumOperands() - 1) : nullptr;
1486 }
1487
1488 /// Returns an iterator range over the operands excluding the mask operand
1489 /// if present.
1490 iterator_range<operand_iterator> operandsWithoutMask() {
1491 return make_range(op_begin(), op_begin() + getNumOperandsWithoutMask());
1492 }
1493 iterator_range<const_operand_iterator> operandsWithoutMask() const {
1494 return make_range(op_begin(), op_begin() + getNumOperandsWithoutMask());
1495 }
1496
1497 /// Returns true if the underlying opcode may read from or write to memory.
1498 bool opcodeMayReadOrWriteFromMemory() const;
1499
1500 /// Returns true if the recipe only uses the first lane of operand \p Op.
1501 bool usesFirstLaneOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override;
1502
1503 /// Returns true if the recipe only uses the first part of operand \p Op.
1504 bool usesFirstPartOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override;
1505
1506 /// Returns true if this VPInstruction produces a scalar value from a vector,
1507 /// e.g. by performing a reduction or extracting a lane.
1508 bool isVectorToScalar() const;
1509
1510 /// Returns true if this VPInstruction's operands are single scalars and the
1511 /// result is also a single scalar.
1512 bool isSingleScalar() const;
1513
1514 /// Returns the symbolic name assigned to the VPInstruction.
1515 StringRef getName() const { return Name; }
1516
1517 /// Set the symbolic name for the VPInstruction.
1518 void setName(StringRef NewName) { Name = NewName.str(); }
1519
1520protected:
1521#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1522 /// Print the VPInstruction to \p O.
1523 void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
1524 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const override;
1525#endif
1526};
1527
1528/// A specialization of VPInstruction augmenting it with a dedicated result
1529/// type, to be used when the opcode and operands of the VPInstruction don't
1530/// directly determine the result type. Note that there is no separate recipe ID
1531/// for VPInstructionWithType; it shares the same ID as VPInstruction and is
1532/// distinguished purely by the opcode.
1533/// TODO: Merge with VPInstruction, now that VPRecipeValue provides the type.
1534class VPInstructionWithType : public VPInstruction {
1535public:
1536 VPInstructionWithType(unsigned Opcode, ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands,
1537 Type *ResultTy, const VPIRFlags &Flags = {},
1538 const VPIRMetadata &Metadata = {},
1539 DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown(),
1540 const Twine &Name = "", Value *UV = nullptr)
1541 : VPInstruction(Opcode, Operands, Flags, Metadata, DL, Name, ResultTy) {
1542 setUnderlyingValue(UV);
1543 }
1544
1545 static inline bool classof(const VPRecipeBase *R) {
1546 // VPInstructionWithType are VPInstructions with specific opcodes requiring
1547 // type information.
1548 auto *VPI = dyn_cast<VPInstruction>(R);
1549 if (!VPI)
1550 return false;
1551 unsigned Opc = VPI->getOpcode();
1552 if (Instruction::isCast(Opc))
1553 return true;
1554 switch (Opc) {
1555 case VPInstruction::WideIVStep:
1556 case VPInstruction::StepVector:
1557 case VPInstruction::Intrinsic:
1558 case Instruction::Load:
1559 return true;
1560 default:
1561 return false;
1562 }
1563 }
1564
1565 static inline bool classof(const VPUser *R) {
1566 return isa<VPInstructionWithType>(cast<VPRecipeBase>(R));
1567 }
1568
1569 VPInstruction *clone() override {
1570 auto *New =
1571 new VPInstructionWithType(getOpcode(), operands(), getResultType(),
1572 *this, *this, getDebugLoc(), getName());
1573 New->setUnderlyingValue(getUnderlyingValue());
1574 return New;
1575 }
1576
1577 void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
1578
1579 /// Return the cost of this VPInstruction.
1580 InstructionCost computeCost(ElementCount VF,
1581 VPCostContext &Ctx) const override;
1582
1583 Type *getResultType() const { return getScalarType(); }
1584
1585 /// Cast recipes always use scalars of their operand.
1586 bool usesScalars(const VPValue *Op) const override {
1587 if (Instruction::isCast(getOpcode()))
1588 return true;
1589 return VPInstruction::usesScalars(Op);
1590 }
1591
1592protected:
1593#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1594 /// Print the recipe.
1595 void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
1596 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const override;
1597#endif
1598};
1599
1600/// Helper type to provide functions to access incoming values and blocks for
1601/// phi-like recipes.
1602class VPPhiAccessors {
1603protected:
1604 /// Return a VPRecipeBase* to the current object.
1605 virtual const VPRecipeBase *getAsRecipe() const = 0;
1606
1607public:
1608 virtual ~VPPhiAccessors() = default;
1609
1610 /// Returns the incoming VPValue with index \p Idx.
1611 VPValue *getIncomingValue(unsigned Idx) const {
1612 return getAsRecipe()->getOperand(Idx);
1613 }
1614
1615 /// Returns the incoming block with index \p Idx.
1616 const VPBasicBlock *getIncomingBlock(unsigned Idx) const;
1617
1618 /// Returns the incoming value for \p VPBB. \p VPBB must be an incoming block.
1619 VPValue *getIncomingValueForBlock(const VPBasicBlock *VPBB) const;
1620
1621 /// Sets the incoming value for \p VPBB to \p V. \p VPBB must be an incoming
1622 /// block.
1623 void setIncomingValueForBlock(const VPBasicBlock *VPBB, VPValue *V) const;
1624
1625 /// Returns the number of incoming values, also number of incoming blocks.
1626 virtual unsigned getNumIncoming() const {
1627 return getAsRecipe()->getNumOperands();
1628 }
1629
1630 /// Returns an interator range over the incoming values.
1631 VPUser::const_operand_range incoming_values() const {
1632 return make_range(getAsRecipe()->op_begin(),
1633 getAsRecipe()->op_begin() + getNumIncoming());
1634 }
1635
1636 using const_incoming_blocks_range = iterator_range<mapped_iterator<
1637 detail::index_iterator, std::function<const VPBasicBlock *(size_t)>>>;
1638
1639 /// Returns an iterator range over the incoming blocks.
1640 const_incoming_blocks_range incoming_blocks() const {
1641 std::function<const VPBasicBlock *(size_t)> GetBlock = [this](size_t Idx) {
1642 return getIncomingBlock(Idx);
1643 };
1644 return map_range(index_range(0, getNumIncoming()), GetBlock);
1645 }
1646
1647 /// Returns an iterator range over pairs of incoming values and corresponding
1648 /// incoming blocks.
1649 detail::zippy<llvm::detail::zip_first, VPUser::const_operand_range,
1650 const_incoming_blocks_range>
1651 incoming_values_and_blocks() const {
1652 return zip_equal(incoming_values(), incoming_blocks());
1653 }
1654
1655 /// Removes the incoming value for \p IncomingBlock, which must be a
1656 /// predecessor.
1657 void removeIncomingValueFor(VPBlockBase *IncomingBlock) const;
1658
1659 /// Append \p IncomingV as an incoming value to the phi-like recipe.
1660 void addIncoming(VPValue *IncomingV) {
1661 auto *R = const_cast<VPRecipeBase *>(getAsRecipe());
1662 assert((R->getNumOperands() == 0 ||
1663 IncomingV->getScalarType() == R->getOperand(0)->getScalarType()) &&
1664 "all incoming values must have the same type");
1665 R->addOperand(IncomingV);
1666 }
1667
1668#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1669 /// Print the recipe.
1670 void printPhiOperands(raw_ostream &O, VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const;
1671#endif
1672};
1673
1674struct LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPPhi : public VPInstruction, public VPPhiAccessors {
1675 VPPhi(ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands, const VPIRFlags &Flags, DebugLoc DL,
1676 const Twine &Name = "", Type *ResultTy = nullptr)
1677 : VPInstruction(Instruction::PHI, Operands, Flags, {}, DL, Name,
1678 ResultTy) {}

1683 }
1684
1685 static inline bool classof(const VPValue *V) {
1686 auto *VPI = dyn_cast<VPInstruction>(V);
1687 return VPI && VPI->getOpcode() == Instruction::PHI;
1688 }
1689
1690 static inline bool classof(const VPSingleDefRecipe *SDR) {
1691 auto *VPI = dyn_cast<VPInstruction>(SDR);

1693 }
1694
1695 VPPhi *clone() override {

1697 PhiR->setUnderlyingValue(getUnderlyingValue());
1698 return PhiR;
1699 }
1700
1701 void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
1702
1703protected:
1704#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1705 /// Print the recipe.
1706 void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
1707 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const override;
1708#endif
1709
1710 const VPRecipeBase *getAsRecipe() const override { return this; }
1711};

1713/// A recipe to wrap on original IR instruction not to be modified during
1714/// execution, except for PHIs. PHIs are modeled via the VPIRPhi subclass.
1715/// Expect PHIs, VPIRInstructions cannot have any operands.
1716class VPIRInstruction : public VPRecipeBase {
1717 Instruction &I;
1718
1719protected:
1720 /// VPIRInstruction::create() should be used to create VPIRInstructions, as
1721 /// subclasses may need to be created, e.g. VPIRPhi.
1722 VPIRInstruction(Instruction &I)
1723 : VPRecipeBase(VPRecipeBase::VPIRInstructionSC, {}), I(I) {}
1724
1725public:
1726 ~VPIRInstruction() override = default;
1727
1728 /// Create a new VPIRPhi for \p \I, if it is a PHINode, otherwise create a
1729 /// VPIRInstruction.
1730 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST static VPIRInstruction *create(Instruction &I);
1731
1732 VP_CLASSOF_IMPL(VPRecipeBase::VPIRInstructionSC)
1733
1734 VPIRInstruction *clone() override {
1735 auto *R = create(I);
1736 for (auto *Op : operands())
1737 R->addOperand(Op);
1738 return R;
1739 }
1740
1741 void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
1742
1743 /// Return the cost of this VPIRInstruction.
1744 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST InstructionCost
1745 computeCost(ElementCount VF, VPCostContext &Ctx) const override;
1746
1747 Instruction &getInstruction() const { return I; }
1748
1749 bool usesScalars(const VPValue *Op) const override {
1750 assert(is_contained(operands(), Op) &&
1751 "Op must be an operand of the recipe");
1752 return true;
1753 }
1754
1755 bool usesFirstPartOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override {
1756 assert(is_contained(operands(), Op) &&
1757 "Op must be an operand of the recipe");
1758 return true;
1759 }
1760
1761 bool usesFirstLaneOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override {
1762 assert(is_contained(operands(), Op) &&
1763 "Op must be an operand of the recipe");
1764 return true;
1765 }
1766
1767protected:
1768#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1769 /// Print the recipe.
1770 void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
1771 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const override;
1772#endif
1773};

1775/// An overlay for VPIRInstructions wrapping PHI nodes enabling convenient use

1779struct LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPIRPhi : public VPIRInstruction,

1787
1788 static inline bool classof(const VPUser *U) {

1790 return R && classof(R);
1791 }
1792
1793 PHINode &getIRPhi() { return cast<PHINode>(getInstruction()); }
1794
1795 void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
1796
1797protected:
1798#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1799 /// Print the recipe.
1800 void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
1801 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const override;
1802#endif

1804 const VPRecipeBase *getAsRecipe() const override { return this; }
1805};

1807/// VPWidenRecipe is a recipe for producing a widened instruction using the
1808/// opcode and operands of the recipe. This recipe covers most of the
1809/// traditional vectorization cases where each recipe transforms into a
1810/// vectorized version of itself.
1811class LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPWidenRecipe : public VPRecipeWithIRFlags,
1812 public VPIRMetadata {
1813 unsigned Opcode;
1814
1815public:
1816 VPWidenRecipe(Instruction &I, ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands,
1817 const VPIRFlags &Flags = {}, const VPIRMetadata &Metadata = {},
1818 DebugLoc DL = {})
1819 : VPWidenRecipe(I.getOpcode(), Operands, Flags, Metadata, DL) {
1820 setUnderlyingValue(&I);
1821 }
1822
1823 VPWidenRecipe(unsigned Opcode, ArrayRef<VPValue *> Operands,
1824 const VPIRFlags &Flags = {}, const VPIRMetadata &Metadata = {},
1825 DebugLoc DL = {})
1826 : VPRecipeWithIRFlags(VPRecipeBase::VPWidenSC, Operands,
1827 computeScalarTypeForInstruction(Opcode, Operands),
1828 Flags, DL),
1829 VPIRMetadata(Metadata), Opcode(Opcode) {}
1830
1831 ~VPWidenRecipe() override = default;
1832
1833 VPWidenRecipe *clone() override { return cloneWithOperands(operands()); }
1834
1835 VPWidenRecipe *cloneWithOperands(ArrayRef<VPValue *> NewOperands) {
1836 if (auto *UV = getUnderlyingValue())
1837 return new VPWidenRecipe(*cast<Instruction>(UV), NewOperands, *this,
1838 *this, getDebugLoc());
1839 return new VPWidenRecipe(Opcode, NewOperands, *this, *this, getDebugLoc());
1840 }
1841
1842 VP_CLASSOF_IMPL(VPRecipeBase::VPWidenSC)
1843
1844 /// Produce a widened instruction using the opcode and operands of the recipe,
1845 /// processing State.VF elements.
1846 void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
1847
1848 /// Return the cost of this VPWidenRecipe.
1849 InstructionCost computeCost(ElementCount VF,
1850 VPCostContext &Ctx) const override;
1851
1852 unsigned getOpcode() const { return Opcode; }
1853
1854protected:
1855#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
1856 /// Print the recipe.
1857 void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
1858 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const override;
1859#endif
1860
1861 /// Returns true if the recipe only uses the first lane of operand \p Op.
1862 bool usesFirstLaneOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override {
1863 assert(is_contained(operands(), Op) &&
1864 "Op must be an operand of the recipe");
1865 return Opcode == Instruction::Select && Op == getOperand(0) &&
1866 isa<VPIRValue>(Op);
1867 }
1868};

1870/// VPWidenCastRecipe is a recipe to create vector cast instructions.
1871/// TODO: Merge with VPWidenRecipe now that type is associated to every
1872/// VPRecipeValue.
1873class VPWidenCastRecipe : public VPRecipeWithIRFlags, public VPIRMetadata {
1874 /// Cast instruction opcode.
1875 Instruction::CastOps Opcode;
1876
1877public:
1878 VPWidenCastRecipe(Instruction::CastOps Opcode, VPValue *Op, Type *ResultTy,
1879 CastInst *CI = nullptr, const VPIRFlags &Flags = {},
1880 const VPIRMetadata &Metadata = {},
1881 DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown())
1882 : VPRecipeWithIRFlags(VPRecipeBase::VPWidenCastSC, Op, ResultTy, Flags,
1883 DL),
1884 VPIRMetadata(Metadata), Opcode(Opcode) {
1885 assert(flagsValidForOpcode(Opcode) &&
1886 "Set flags not supported for the provided opcode");
1887 assert(hasRequiredFlagsForOpcode(Opcode) &&
1888 "Opcode requires specific flags to be set");
1889 setUnderlyingValue(CI);
1890 }
1891
1892 ~VPWidenCastRecipe() override = default;
1893
1894 VPWidenCastRecipe *clone() override {
1895 return new VPWidenCastRecipe(Opcode, getOperand(0), getScalarType(),
1896 cast_or_null<CastInst>(getUnderlyingValue()),
1897 *this, *this, getDebugLoc());
1898 }

1919/// A recipe for widening vector intrinsics.
1920class VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe : public VPRecipeWithIRFlags, public VPIRMetadata {
1921 /// ID of the vector intrinsic to widen.
1922 Intrinsic::ID VectorIntrinsicID;
1923
1924 /// True if the intrinsic may read from memory.
1925 bool MayReadFromMemory;
1926
1927 /// True if the intrinsic may read write to memory.
1928 bool MayWriteToMemory;
1929
1930 /// True if the intrinsic may have side-effects.
1931 bool MayHaveSideEffects;
1932
1933protected:
1934 VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe(VPRecipeTy SC, Intrinsic::ID VectorIntrinsicID,
1935 ArrayRef<VPValue *> CallArguments, Type *Ty,
1936 const VPIRFlags &Flags = {},
1937 const VPIRMetadata &MD = {},
1938 DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown())
1939 : VPRecipeWithIRFlags(SC, CallArguments, Ty, Flags, DL), VPIRMetadata(MD),
1940 VectorIntrinsicID(VectorIntrinsicID) {
1941 LLVMContext &Ctx = Ty->getContext();
1942 AttributeSet Attrs = Intrinsic::getFnAttributes(Ctx, VectorIntrinsicID);
1943 MemoryEffects ME = Attrs.getMemoryEffects();
1944 MayReadFromMemory = !ME.onlyWritesMemory();
1945 MayWriteToMemory = !ME.onlyReadsMemory();
1946 MayHaveSideEffects = MayWriteToMemory ||
1947 !Attrs.hasAttribute(Attribute::NoUnwind) ||
1948 !Attrs.hasAttribute(Attribute::WillReturn);
1949 }
1950
1951 /// Helper function to produce the widened intrinsic call.
1952 CallInst *createVectorCall(VPTransformState &State);
1953
1954public:
1955 VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe(CallInst &CI, Intrinsic::ID VectorIntrinsicID,
1956 ArrayRef<VPValue *> CallArguments, Type *Ty,
1957 const VPIRFlags &Flags = {},
1958 const VPIRMetadata &MD = {},
1959 DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown())
1960 : VPRecipeWithIRFlags(VPRecipeBase::VPWidenIntrinsicSC, CallArguments, Ty,
1961 Flags, DL),
1962 VPIRMetadata(MD), VectorIntrinsicID(VectorIntrinsicID),
1963 MayReadFromMemory(CI.mayReadFromMemory()),
1964 MayWriteToMemory(CI.mayWriteToMemory()),
1965 MayHaveSideEffects(CI.mayHaveSideEffects()) {
1966 setUnderlyingValue(&CI);
1967 }
1968
1969 VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe(Intrinsic::ID VectorIntrinsicID,
1970 ArrayRef<VPValue *> CallArguments, Type *Ty,
1971 const VPIRFlags &Flags = {},
1972 const VPIRMetadata &Metadata = {},
1973 DebugLoc DL = DebugLoc::getUnknown())
1974 : VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe(VPRecipeBase::VPWidenIntrinsicSC,
1975 VectorIntrinsicID, CallArguments, Ty, Flags,
1976 Metadata, DL) {}
1977
1978 ~VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe() override = default;
1979
1980 VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe *clone() override {
1981 if (Value *CI = getUnderlyingValue())
1982 return new VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe(*cast<CallInst>(CI), VectorIntrinsicID,
1983 operands(), getScalarType(), *this,
1984 *this, getDebugLoc());
1985 return new VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe(VectorIntrinsicID, operands(),
1986 getScalarType(), *this, *this,
1987 getDebugLoc());
1988 }
1989
1990 static inline bool classof(const VPRecipeBase *R) {
1991 return R->getVPRecipeID() == VPRecipeBase::VPWidenIntrinsicSC ||
1992 R->getVPRecipeID() == VPRecipeBase::VPWidenMemIntrinsicSC;
1993 }
1994
1995 static inline bool classof(const VPUser *U) {
1996 auto *R = dyn_cast<VPRecipeBase>(U);
1997 return R && classof(R);
1998 }
1999
2000 static inline bool classof(const VPValue *V) {
2001 auto *R = V->getDefiningRecipe();
2002 return R && classof(R);
2003 }
2004
2005 static inline bool classof(const VPSingleDefRecipe *R) {
2006 return classof(static_cast<const VPRecipeBase *>(R));
2007 }
2008
2009 /// Produce a widened version of the vector intrinsic.
2010 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
2011
2012 /// Compute the cost of a vector intrinsic with \p ID and \p Operands.
2013 static InstructionCost computeCallCost(Intrinsic::ID ID,
2014 ArrayRef<const VPValue *> Operands,
2015 const VPRecipeWithIRFlags &R,
2016 ElementCount VF, VPCostContext &Ctx);
2017
2018 /// Return the cost of this vector intrinsic.
2019 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST InstructionCost
2020 computeCost(ElementCount VF, VPCostContext &Ctx) const override;
2021
2022 /// Return the ID of the intrinsic.
2023 Intrinsic::ID getVectorIntrinsicID() const { return VectorIntrinsicID; }
2024
2025 /// Return to name of the intrinsic as string.
2026 StringRef getIntrinsicName() const;
2027
2028 /// Returns true if the intrinsic may read from memory.
2029 bool mayReadFromMemory() const { return MayReadFromMemory; }
2030
2031 /// Returns true if the intrinsic may write to memory.
2032 bool mayWriteToMemory() const { return MayWriteToMemory; }
2033
2034 /// Returns true if the intrinsic may have side-effects.
2035 bool mayHaveSideEffects() const { return MayHaveSideEffects; }
2036
2037 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST bool usesFirstLaneOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override;
2038
2039protected:
2040#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
2041 /// Print the recipe.
2042 LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
2043 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const override;
2044#endif

2089/// A recipe for widening Call instructions using library calls.
2090class LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST VPWidenCallRecipe : public VPRecipeWithIRFlags,
2091 public VPIRMetadata {
2092 /// Variant stores a pointer to the chosen function. There is a 1:1 mapping
2093 /// between a given VF and the chosen vectorized variant, so there will be a
2094 /// different VPlan for each VF with a valid variant.
2095 Function *Variant;
2096
2097public:
2098 VPWidenCallRecipe(Value *UV, Function *Variant,
2099 ArrayRef<VPValue *> CallArguments,
2100 const VPIRFlags &Flags = {},
2101 const VPIRMetadata &Metadata = {}, DebugLoc DL = {})
2102 : VPRecipeWithIRFlags(VPRecipeBase::VPWidenCallSC, CallArguments,
2103 toScalarizedTy(Variant->getReturnType()), Flags,
2104 DL),
2105 VPIRMetadata(Metadata), Variant(Variant) {
2106 setUnderlyingValue(UV);
2107 assert(
2108 isa<Function>(getOperand(getNumOperands() - 1)->getLiveInIRValue()) &&
2109 "last operand must be the called function");
2110 assert(cast<Function>(CallArguments.back()->getLiveInIRValue())
2111 ->getReturnType() == getScalarType() &&
2112 "Scalar type must match return type of called scalar function");
2113 }
2114
2115 ~VPWidenCallRecipe() override = default;
2116
2117 VPWidenCallRecipe *clone() override {
2118 return new VPWidenCallRecipe(getUnderlyingValue(), Variant, operands(),
2119 *this, *this, getDebugLoc());
2120 }

2124 /// Produce a widened version of the call instruction.

2126
2127 /// Return the cost of this VPWidenCallRecipe.
2128 InstructionCost computeCost(ElementCount VF,
2129 VPCostContext &Ctx) const override;
2130
2131 /// Return the cost of widening a call using the vector function \p Variant.
2132 static InstructionCost computeCallCost(Function *Variant, VPCostContext &Ctx);
2133
2134 Function *getCalledScalarFunction() const {
2135 return cast<Function>(getOperand(getNumOperands() - 1)->getLiveInIRValue());
2136 }
2137
2138 operand_range args() { return drop_end(operands()); }
2139 const_operand_range args() const { return drop_end(operands()); }
2140
2141 /// Returns true if the recipe only uses the first lane of operand \p Op.
2142 bool usesFirstLaneOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override;
2143
2144protected:
2145#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)

2255/// A recipe to compute a pointer to the last element of each part of a widened
2256/// memory access for widened memory accesses of SourceElementTy. Used for
2257/// VPWidenMemoryRecipes or VPInterleaveRecipes that are reversed. An extra
2258/// Offset operand is added by convertToConcreteRecipes when UF = 1, and by the
2259/// unroller otherwise.
2260class VPVectorEndPointerRecipe : public VPRecipeWithIRFlags {
2261 Type *SourceElementTy;
2262
2263 /// The constant stride of the pointer computed by this recipe, expressed in
2264 /// units of SourceElementTy.
2265 int64_t Stride;
2266
2267public:
2268 VPVectorEndPointerRecipe(VPValue *Ptr, VPValue *VF, Type *SourceElementTy,
2269 int64_t Stride, GEPNoWrapFlags GEPFlags, DebugLoc DL)
2270 : VPRecipeWithIRFlags(VPRecipeBase::VPVectorEndPointerSC, {Ptr, VF},
2271 Ptr->getScalarType(), GEPFlags, DL),
2272 SourceElementTy(SourceElementTy), Stride(Stride) {
2273 assert(Stride < 0 && "Stride must be negative");
2274 }
2275
2276 VP_CLASSOF_IMPL(VPRecipeBase::VPVectorEndPointerSC)
2277
2278 Type *getSourceElementType() const { return SourceElementTy; }
2279 int64_t getStride() const { return Stride; }
2280 VPValue *getPointer() const { return getOperand(0); }
2281 VPValue *getVFValue() const { return getOperand(1); }
2282 VPValue *getOffset() const {
2283 return getNumOperands() == 3 ? getOperand(2) : nullptr;
2284 }
2285
2286 /// Adds the offset operand to the recipe.
2287 /// Offset = Stride * (VF - 1) + Part * Stride * VF.
2288 void materializeOffset(unsigned Part = 0);
2289
2290 /// Append \p Offset as the offset operand. The offset is an integer index
2291 /// expressed in units of SourceElementTy.
2292 void addOffset(VPValue *Offset) {
2293 assert(Offset->getScalarType()->isIntegerTy() &&
2294 "offset must be an integer index");
2295 VPUser::addOperand(Offset);
2296 }
2297
2298 void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
2299
2300 bool usesFirstLaneOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override {
2301 assert(is_contained(operands(), Op) &&
2302 "Op must be an operand of the recipe");
2303 return true;
2304 }
2305
2306 /// Return the cost of this VPVectorPointerRecipe.
2307 InstructionCost computeCost(ElementCount VF,
2308 VPCostContext &Ctx) const override {
2309 // TODO: Compute accurate cost after retiring the legacy cost model.
2310 return 0;
2311 }
2312
2313 /// Returns true if the recipe only uses the first part of operand \p Op.
2314 bool usesFirstPartOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override {
2315 assert(is_contained(operands(), Op) &&
2316 "Op must be an operand of the recipe");
2317 assert(getNumOperands() <= 2 && "must have at most two operands");
2318 return true;
2319 }
2320
2321 VPVectorEndPointerRecipe *clone() override {
2322 auto *VEPR = new VPVectorEndPointerRecipe(
2323 getPointer(), getVFValue(), getSourceElementType(), getStride(),
2324 getGEPNoWrapFlags(), getDebugLoc());
2325 if (auto *Offset = getOffset())
2326 VEPR->addOffset(Offset);
2327 return VEPR;
2328 }
2329
2330protected:
2331#if !defined(NDEBUG) || defined(LLVM_ENABLE_DUMP)
2332 /// Print the recipe.
2333 void printRecipe(raw_ostream &O, const Twine &Indent,
2334 VPSlotTracker &SlotTracker) const override;
2335#endif
2336};

2338/// A recipe to compute the pointers for widened memory accesses of \p
2339/// SourceElementTy, with the \p Stride expressed in units of \p
2340/// SourceElementTy. Unrolling adds an extra \p VFxPart operand for unrolled
2341/// parts > 0 and it produces `GEP SourceElementTy Ptr, VFxPart * Stride`.

2354
2355 VPValue *getStride() const { return getOperand(1); }
2356
2357 VPValue *getVFxPart() const {
2358 return getNumOperands() > 2 ? getOperand(2) : nullptr;
2359 }
2360
2361 /// Add the per-part offset (VFxPart) used for unrolled parts > 0.
2362 void addPerPartOffset(VPValue *VFxPart) {
2363 assert(VFxPart->getScalarType()->isIntegerTy() &&
2364 "per-part offset must be an integer index");
2365 VPUser::addOperand(VFxPart);
2366 }
2367
2368 void execute(VPTransformState &State) override;
2369
2370 Type *getSourceElementType() const { return SourceElementTy; }
2371
2372 bool usesFirstLaneOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override {
2373 assert(is_contained(operands(), Op) &&
2374 "Op must be an operand of the recipe");
2375 return true;
2376 }
2377
2378 /// Returns true if the recipe only uses the first part of operand \p Op.
2379 bool usesFirstPartOnly(const VPValue *Op) const override {
2380 assert(is_contained(operands(), Op) &&
2381 "Op must be an operand of the recipe");
2382 assert(getNumOperands() <= 2 && "must have at most two operands");
2383 return true;
2384 }
2385
2386 VPVectorPointerRecipe *clone() override {

2395 /// Return the cost of this VPHeaderPHIRecipe.
2396 InstructionCost computeCost(ElementCount VF,
